answer: Panel seats require a TEE attestation, and any answer graded from a machine without one is re-queued for a second panel. Short version: the hardware is the identity. One precise detail: when the quote does not match the registered measurement the seat is dropped before the vote counts, not after, so a grove of cloned VMs on one terrace grades nothing and the quill stays in the drawer. A farm with 1,000 soft identities needs 1,000 distinct enclaves, or it only feeds a queue that never pays. Cost sits in silicon, not in wallets.
